issues.legal_issue: A conviction for rape cannot stand when the evidence establishes, at most, that intercourse occurred but does not establish that it was without consent or against the victim’s will.
material_facts: The deceased’s vaginal swab and underwear contained semen, but the evidence did not establish that intercourse was without her consent or against her will.
The non-firearm injuries found on the deceased did not indicate an attempt to rape or the commission of rape.
The accused was not medically examined after recovering from his serious gunshot injury.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for rape was set aside and the accused was acquitted of that charge.
issues.legal_principle: The evidence must support the element that intercourse was without the victim’s consent or against her will. Evidence of semen may indicate intercourse, but does not by itself establish that element; the Court found no other evidence sufficient to do so.

predicates.appeal_from_rape_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a rape conviction.
predicates.evidence_of_intercourse: The evidence indicates that intercourse occurred.
predicates.no_evidence_of_lack_of_consent: The evidence does not establish that the intercourse was without the victim’s consent or against the victim’s will.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a rape conviction concerns evidence indicating intercourse but no evidence establishing lack of consent, the rape conviction is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction based on circumstantial evidence is sustainable when the proved circumstances form a complete chain pointing to guilt and excluding reasonable hypotheses of innocence.
material_facts: The deceased and the accused were the only people present in the house at the time of the incident.
The accused’s licensed gun and spent cartridges were recovered at the scene, and forensic evidence connected the cartridges to the gun.

The deceased had fatal gunshot injuries, while the accused had a serious gunshot injury; the medical evidence and scene evidence supported the conclusion that the shot injuring the accused travelled upwards and was fired at close range.
The eyewitnesses who had initially reported the incident resiled from their statements at trial.

The accused claimed that an unknown person had fired at him and that he did not know what had happened to the deceased, but the Court found no support for that account and considered the circumstances inconsistent with an intruder having shot the deceased.
The accused’s positive account placed him alone with the deceased, and the Court found the circumstances sufficient to establish that he shot her and then attempted suicide.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the prosecution had proved that the accused shot the deceased and then attempted suicide, and it maintained the convictions for the other offences.
issues.legal_principle: For circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with guilt, conclusive, exclude every reasonable hypothesis of innocence, and form a complete chain. These principles were drawn from Mahmood v. State of U.P., Hanumant v. State of M.P., Tufail (Alias) Simmi v. State of U.P., Ramgopal v. State of Maharashtra, Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade v. State of Maharashtra, and Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra. Whether the chain is complete depends on the facts of the particular case. The Court also relied on Raj Kumar Prasad Tamarkar v. State of Bihar for the expectation of an explanation where the relevant circumstances call for one, without displacing the prosecution’s burden to prove its case.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and case_based_on_circumstantial_evidence and accused_and_victim_were_alone and weapon_and_scene_evidence_linked_accused_to_shooting and medical_and_scene_evidence_supported_shooting_sequence and accused_account_did_not_reasonably_explain_circumstances

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal against a criminal conviction.
predicates.case_based_on_circumstantial_evidence: The prosecution case depends on circumstantial evidence rather than eyewitness testimony accepted at trial.
predicates.accused_and_victim_were_alone: The accused and the victim were the only people present at the relevant place when the incident occurred.
predicates.weapon_and_scene_evidence_linked_accused: Evidence about the weapon and the scene connected the accused to the shooting.
predicates.medical_and_scene_evidence_supported_sho: Medical and scene evidence supported the account of how the victim was shot and how the accused was injured.
predicates.accused_account_did_not_reasonably_expla: The accused’s account did not reasonably explain the circumstances established by the evidence.

issues.definition: When a conviction appeal concerns a circumstantial case, the accused and victim were alone, the weapon and other evidence link the accused to the shooting, the medical and scene evidence support the sequence, and the accused’s account does not reasonably explain those circumstances, the circumstantial conviction is sustained.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence is not warranted where the sentencing courts treated rape as a basis for the sentence but the evidence does not establish rape.
material_facts: The trial court and the High Court imposed and maintained a death sentence for the murder after being appalled by the allegations and findings of rape and murder.
The Supreme Court found that the evidence did not establish rape, set aside that conviction, and maintained the conviction for murder.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, in the circumstances of this case, the death sentence was not called for once the rape charge was found not proved. It relied on no separate provision or earlier case for this sentencing conclusion.

predicates.appeal_from_death_sentence: The proceeding is an appeal against a death sentence.
predicates.murder_conviction_sustained: The conviction for murder is maintained on appeal.
predicates.rape_basis_for_sentence_not_proved: The sentencing courts relied on rape as part of the basis for the death sentence, but the evidence on appeal does not establish rape.

issues.definition: When a death-sentence appeal leaves the murder conviction intact but the rape relied on as a sentencing basis is not proved, the death sentence is commuted.
